knowledge:
- key_parameters: dbr=Expected doublet rate. If omitted, it is automatically estimated for 10x data based on cell count ;; dbr.per1k=Expected doublet rate per 1000 cells (default is 0.008 for standard 10x, use 0.004 for 10x HT) ;; dbr.sd=Standard deviation around dbr; setting dbr.sd=1 bases thresholding entirely on misclassification rate without assuming a fixed doublet rate ;; clusters=Vector of cluster labels, colData column name, or TRUE (uses fastcluster) to enable cluster-based doublet generation ;; samples=Vector of sample/capture IDs or colData column name; crucial for multi-sample datasets to prevent overestimating doublet rates ;; artificialDoublets=Number of artificial doublets to generate (defaults to roughly the number of cells) ;; BPPARAM=BiocParallel parameter for multithreading (e.g., MulticoreParam(3)) ;; processing=Custom function for normalization and PCA of combined real and artificial cells
- alternatives: computeDoubletDensity=Density-based method (formerly scran::doubletCells) that scores cells based on the local density of simulated doublets in PCA space; use when a simple, fast, non-classifier approach is preferred ;; recoverDoublets=Use when some doublets are already known (e.g., via cell hashing or SNPs) to find neighboring intra-sample doublets ;; findDoubletClusters=Cluster-level doublet detection using differential expression and intermediacy testing; use when you want to identify entire clusters that are likely doublets ;; directDblClassification=Classifier trained directly on gene expression; generally worse and slower than scDblFinder, included chiefly for comparative purposes
- when_to_use: Appropriate during the preprocessing/QC stage of single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq analysis, after removing empty droplets but before downstream clustering and cell-type annotation, to identify and remove heterotypic doublets.
- pitfalls: Not splitting multi-sample datasets using the samples argument, which causes scDblFinder to assume a single massive capture and overestimate the doublet rate ;; Running QC cell filtering (like removing low-quality cells) too stringently before doublet detection, which can skew the expected doublet rate and prevent detection of doublets formed by a high-quality and a low-quality cell ;; Using the cluster-based approach or leaving removeUnidentifiable=TRUE when trying to identify homotypic doublets (which are transcriptionally similar and typically filtered out of training) ;; Failing to pass the random seed to BPPARAM (e.g., RNGseed) when running multi-sample or multithreaded analyses, leading to non-reproducible results ;; Cells with zero or very low read counts causing "Size factors should be positive" errors; these must be filtered out first.

workflows.name: sc_dbl_finder
workflows.intent: Run the main scDblFinder workflow on a SingleCellExperiment object to score and classify doublets.
input: sce.rds (SingleCellExperiment object containing raw count matrix in 'counts' assay)
workflows.stages: 1. Set random seed for reproducibility ;; 2. Run scDblFinder with optional doublet rate (dbr), cluster information (clusters), or sample splitting (samples) ;; 3. Inspect results in colData (scDblFinder.score and scDblFinder.class)
workflows.code:
set.seed(123)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(scDblFinder))
# we create a dummy dataset; since it's small we set a higher doublet rate
sce <- mockDoubletSCE(dbl.rate=0.1, ngenes=300 )
# we run scDblFinder (providing the unusually high doublet rate)
sce <- scDblFinder(sce, dbr=0.1)
sce <- scDblFinder(sce, clusters="cluster")
library(BiocParallel)
sce <- scDblFinder(sce, samples="sample_id", BPPARAM=MulticoreParam(3))
bp <- MulticoreParam(3, RNGseed=1234)
sce <- scDblFinder(sce, clusters="cluster", samples="sample", BPPARAM=bp)

workflows.name: find_doublet_clusters
workflows.intent: Identify entire clusters that are likely composed of doublets by testing for lack of intermediacy in expression profiles.
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize counts using logNormCounts ;; 2. Model gene variance and run PCA ;; 3. Cluster cells using clusterRows ;; 4. Run findDoubletClusters to test each cluster against the doublet null hypothesis
workflows.code:
library(scRNAseq)
sce <- BachMammaryData(samples="G_2")
set.seed(1000)
sce <- sce[,sample(ncol(sce), 500)]
library(scuttle)
sce <- logNormCounts(sce)
library(scran)
dec <- modelGeneVar(sce)
library(scater)
set.seed(1000)
sce <- runPCA(sce, ncomponents=10, subset_row=getTopHVGs(dec, n=1000))
library(bluster)
clusters <- clusterRows(reducedDim(sce, "PCA"), NNGraphParam())
sce <- runTSNE(sce, dimred="PCA")
plotTSNE(sce, colour_by=I(clusters), text_by=I(clusters))
library(scDblFinder)
tab <- findDoubletClusters(sce, clusters)

workflows.name: compute_doublet_density
workflows.intent: Score potential doublets based on the local density of simulated doublets in PCA space.
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize counts and identify highly variable genes ;; 2. Run PCA ;; 3. Run computeDoubletDensity to calculate doublet scores
workflows.code:
library(scRNAseq)
sce <- BachMammaryData(samples="G_1")
set.seed(1001)
sce <- sce[,sample(ncol(sce), 1000)]
library(scuttle)
sce <- logNormCounts(sce)
library(scran)
dec <- modelGeneVar(sce)
hvgs <- getTopHVGs(dec, n=1000)
library(scater)
set.seed(1002)
sce <- runPCA(sce, ncomponents=10, subset_row=hvgs)
sce <- runTSNE(sce, dimred="PCA")
set.seed(1003)
library(scDblFinder)
scores <- computeDoubletDensity(sce, subset.row=hvgs)
plotTSNE(sce, colour_by=I(log1p(scores)))
